title: Bernoulli check of Hoeffding's one-sided inequality (independent implementation)
objective: Simulate independent Bernoulli(p) samples at several sample sizes and compare the empirical one-sided tail probability with Hoeffding's finite-sample bound and with the exact binomial tail.
paperResult: Hoeffding's inequality bounds the upper tail of a sum of independent bounded variables. For Xi in [0,1] and Xbar = (X1 + ... + Xn)/n, Pr[Xbar - E[Xbar] >= epsilon] <= exp(-2 n epsilon^2). For Bernoulli(p), E[Xbar] = p, so the demo compares the simulated frequency of successes/n - p >= epsilon against exp(-2 n epsilon^2) and the exact binomial tail. The source is an expository report that restates Hoeffding's theorem; no published numeric value from it is being reproduced.

sourceRefs.quote: Hoeffding’s inequality provides an upper bound on the probability that the sum of independent random variables deviates from its expected value by more than a certain amount.
By adding them both up, we can obtain two-sided variant of this inequality

data.description: No external dataset. For each sample size n, generate trials_per_n independent samples of n Bernoulli(p) draws at runtime from the fixed integer seed using a seeded deterministic pseudorandom generator. samples.csv records every trial's success count, so the primary metric can be recomputed from the data alone.
data.split: None. Each row is one independent repetition; different n values use independent draws from the same seeded stream.
data.preprocessing: None. Count successes in each sample; p and epsilon are the declared constants.

method: For each n in n_values, run trials_per_n repetitions. In repetition trial, draw exactly n Bernoulli(p) values with a deterministic seeded generator, count successes, and mark the one-sided event successes/n - p >= epsilon (integer threshold ceil(n*(p+epsilon)-1e-12)). The empirical tail probability is the fraction of marked repetitions. Compare it with Hoeffding's bound exp(-2*n*epsilon^2) and with the exact binomial upper tail at the same threshold. Report Monte Carlo standard error and the maximum empirical-minus-bound difference across all configured n.
baseline: Hoeffding's analytic bound exp(-2*n*epsilon^2) and the exact one-sided binomial tail at the same integer threshold; both are computed without reading the simulated metric back.

metric.name: empirical_tail_probability
metric.computation: At primary_n, count rows in samples.csv with successes >= ceil(n*(p+epsilon)-1e-12), divide by trials_per_n. Independently recompute the same value from the CSV counts; never read the metric back from metrics.json. Also report hoeffding_bound = exp(-2*n*epsilon^2), exact_binomial_tail_probability, their differences, Monte Carlo standard error, and max_empirical_minus_bound across n.

assumptions: The cited arXiv report is an expository restatement of Hoeffding's 1963 theorem, not the source of the simulation. The simulation is an independent reimplementation, not author code.
Observations are independent and identically distributed Bernoulli(p) with known p; each repetition uses exactly n draws.
The tail event is one-sided: successes/n - p >= epsilon, using the integer threshold ceil(n*(p+epsilon)-1e-12) to avoid floating-point boundary ambiguity.

The Hoeffding bound applies to the true tail probability. The empirical fraction is a finite Monte Carlo estimate with reported standard error; an empirical value above the bound is not by itself a theorem violation.
The seed makes the reference baseline repeatable, but a single artifact set cannot prove that an arbitrary worker's generator was deterministic.
No published numeric value is reproduced and no claim of reproducing the paper's empirical results is made.
